title: Build and publish a simple web tool from one prompt
summary: A developer gave Cursor a detailed spec written with Claude's help; it built and published a dollar-and-peso tip calculator, which they say went live in eight minutes.
agent_role: Cursor wrote the single-file app and README, ran git init, created the repo with gh and enabled Pages. The human revised the spec, tested the math by hand and had Claude review the code afterwards.
outcome: Author reports eight minutes from first ask to a live site, with one commit and no redirects. A Claude review found a fractional-people bug and a missing aria-live attribute, fixed in two lines.
what_they_did: The author asked Claude to draft instructions for building the tool. They then edited it to ask for US dollars and Mexican pesos, exact brand colors and fonts, and checks on what users type. It also said the tool must never show an error number and must not add features beyond the list. They pasted this into Cursor. It also told the agent to save the work, create a public project on GitHub and publish it as a free web page there.
how_it_went: They say the site was live eight minutes after the first ask, from one save with no corrections. A later review by Claude of the 424-line file found two problems. It accepted 1.5 people, and screen readers for blind users got no updates. Both were fixed in a second save with two lines changed.
worth_knowing: The author credits the speed to the detailed instructions, not the tool. Every design choice was made before Cursor started, and the line forbidding extra features did a lot of the work.
prompt: Build a [small app, e.g. tip calculator] as a single index.html with inline CSS and JS, no frameworks. Requirements: [inputs, outputs, validation rules, never show NaN, use textContent]. Style: [your colors and fonts]. Add a short README. Do not add features beyond this list. Then show me the plan for git init, creating a public GitHub repo named [repo name] with gh, pushing and enabling GitHub Pages. Wait for my approval before creating or publishing anything, then give me the repo and Pages links.

curation.rationale: A small, well-documented build with a verbatim prompt and a timeline, where Cursor built, committed and deployed the app. A tip calculator is a derivative example, though the spec-first lesson is useful.
